Thanks Ava — got the spreadsheet and the context. We'll come to kickoff with a recommended regional footprint and a draft autoscale/burst policy tailored to your diurnal curve. High-level notes up front:

- If 85% of traffic is US-based, we generally recommend a single primary US region (us-west for lower cost if your customers are West-heavy; us-east if you need east coast latency) and a cross-region warm standby in eu-west only if you plan EU traffic growth or need compliance isolation.
- Bursting model: reserve a baseline pool sized for steady-state + scheduled autoscale for sustained ramps; short promotional spikes are best served by burst capacity (pre-warmed GPUs or fast allocation policy) tied to time windows.
- We'll need expected sustained qps, peak token/sec per minute, and any network egress constraints. The attached SLO/proposal will include suggested pre-warm thresholds.

Can you confirm Thu 9/9 10:00 PT for a 60-minute kickoff?

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
